title: Global AI Regulations for FAIR and Ethics in High-Risk Use Cases: A Comparative Review
abstract: arXiv:2608.14562v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI governance is shifting from voluntary ethics to enforceable, risk-based regulation, yet cross-jurisdictional divergence creates compliance uncertainty for operators of high-stakes AI. We present a comparative matrix for the EU, US, and China that maps (i) risk classification triggers, (ii) binding obligations, (iii) enforcement and accountability mechanisms, and (iv) the degree to which FAIR principles are operationalised in practice. translated_title: 全球高风险应用场景中公平与伦理的AI监管：一项比较性审查
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14562v1 公告类型：新 摘要：AI治理正从自愿伦理规范转向可执行的、基于风险的监管，但跨司法管辖区的差异给高风险AI运营者带来了合规不确定性。我们为欧盟、美国和中国构建了一个比较矩阵，该矩阵映射了（i）风险分类触发条件，（ii）约束性义务，（iii）执法与问责机制，以及（iv）FAIR原则在实践中被落实的程度。我们在三个高影响领域对该矩阵进行了压力测试：脑电图（EEG）引导的康复机器人、预期央行数字货币（CBDC）生态系统中的AI辅助债务催收，以及新兴AI工厂基础设施中AI驱动的稀缺图形处理器（GPU）资源分配。基于原始法律文本和实施证据，我们识别出三个反复出现的缺口：互操作性授权薄弱、跨制度义务（AI+）难以实际执行。
tldr: 本文通过比较欧盟、美国和中国的AI监管框架，揭示了高风险应用中FAIR原则落实不足和跨辖区合规的三大关键缺口。
en_tdlr: This paper compares AI regulatory frameworks in the EU, US, and China, identifying three key gaps in FAIR principle implementation and cross-jurisdictional compliance for high-risk applications.
